definition: dwell unhappily on a thought; also a group of young birds
memoryTip: Like a hen brooding — sit and stew on dark thoughts (or a clutch of chicks).
correctPassage: He continued to brood over the failed trial long after the rest of the team had moved on.
wrongPassages: She brooded over the invitation by accepting it at once and arriving early to help set up.
Once the problem was solved, they brooded cheerfully over their success around the table.
The panel brooded the agenda item for two minutes, then approved it without further comment.

definition: deep respect, often tinged with awe
memoryTip: Revere someone — treat them with deep, almost sacred respect.
correctPassage: Visitors approached the manuscript with a reverence reserved for rare and fragile objects.
wrongPassages: Critics praised his reverence for the score, which he rearranged freely without consulting the original markings.
The class showed reverence for the guest lecturer by talking through most of her presentation.
She expressed reverence for the collection by handling the oldest volumes without gloves.

definition: serving as a desirable model; outstandingly good
memoryTip: Worthy to be an example — model behavior others should copy.
correctPassage: Her laboratory notebooks are exemplary in their clarity and care.
wrongPassages: Reviewers called the draft exemplary, citing its incomplete citations and unsupported claims.
His exemplary attendance record listed more absences than any other student in the course.
The board held up the delayed, over-budget project as exemplary of how future initiatives should run.

definition: openly resist or refuse to obey; go against
memoryTip: De-fy: refuse to bow — openly resist an order or expectation.
correctPassage: The results appear to defy the predictions of the standard model.
wrongPassages: She chose to defy the curfew by returning home well before the deadline each night.
The class decided to defy the instructor by following the assigned outline section by section.
He managed to defy the ban by securing every required permit before the event began.

definition: important or relevant (as in material evidence)
memoryTip: Matters materially — important/relevant, not just “stuff” you can touch.
correctPassage: Only material differences between the samples were reported in the abstract.
wrongPassages: The judge called the typo material to the verdict, noting that it changed nothing about the evidence.
Counsel argued that a material fact was one the jury could safely set aside.
Researchers labeled the discrepancy material precisely because it had no bearing on the conclusions.
